title: Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One
abstract: arXiv:2611.20826v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The claim that interactions with artificial conversational agents merely simulate human conversation rests on a philosophical distinction between reproducing the observable features of an activity and actually performing it. Although this distinction is appropriate for certain physical phenomena, its application to linguistic and symbolic activities is far less straightforward. This article argues that conversations with large language model (LLM)-based agents are genuine conversational activities rather than mere simulations, without thereby attributing consciousness, subjective understanding, or human intentionality to artificial systems. Drawing on the distinction between subjective and objective simulation, the article first examines the limitations of defining conversation exclusively through the intrinsic properties of its participants. translated_title: 与会话代理对话：一场真实的对话，而非模拟的对话
translated_abstract: “与人工会话代理的交互仅仅是在模拟人类对话”这一主张，建立在“再现某一活动的可观察特征”与“实际执行该活动”之间的哲学区分之上。尽管这一区分适用于某些物理现象，但将其应用于语言和符号活动则远非如此直接。本文论证，与基于大语言模型（LLM）的代理进行的对话是真实的对话活动，而非仅仅是模拟，同时并不因此将意识、主观理解或人类意向性归于人工系统。借助主观模拟与客观模拟之间的区分，本文首先考察了仅通过参与者内在属性来定义对话的局限性，随后发展了一种基于关系性视角和符号学的对话活动理论。
tldr: 本文从关系性与符号学视角论证，与大语言模型代理的对话是真实的对话活动而非单纯模拟，且这一论证无需将意识或主观理解归于人工智能系统。
en_tdlr: This paper argues from a relational and semiotic perspective that conversations with LLM-based agents are genuine conversational activities rather than mere simulations, without attributing consciousness or subjective understanding to artificial systems.
